body:
State saved, coherence confirmed, latest files sent (TUNGSTEN 10.06/SLS(92) source+ex4, ledger
pass_88). Plus: forge-organism v7 installed and WARRANT#107 shipped.

Coherence check before sending: working-copy source is byte-identical to what's deployed in the
terminal's Experts folder, the compiled .ex4 is fresh off the latest edit in both places, version
tags (10.06/SLS(92)) match everywhere including inside the ratchet-log fix from earlier, and the
ledger copy in MQL4/Files matches the working copy exactly. All three files then sent to the
mailbox as real attachments.

FORGE_ORGANISM_CHARTER_v7.md installed: v6 was never actually delivered (same gap as a couple of
other lineage references this campaign has hit -- flagged, not invented). v7 keeps everything v5
built (the portal/probability-conversion work, the 11-class defect taxonomy, the boundary audit)
and adds one real new idea: your fourteen intel layers agreeing with each other (confluence) should
detect a good entry faster and more reliably than just waiting for price alone to confirm -- but
ONLY if those layers are genuinely independent of each other, not just re-deriving the same price
information three different ways. The charter is explicit its own supporting numbers come from the
author's synthetic test model, not from TUNGSTEN, so none of that is treated as proven here.

Before building anything, checked what already exists: forge-indicate's relationship-tracking
machinery (from earlier this campaign) already measures almost exactly what v7 asks for in its
indicator-profiling step -- whether pairs of indicators agreeing actually predicts a better outcome
than when they conflict -- it's just never been summarized as "which indicators have earned a
vote." WARRANT#107 added that summary using only data already being computed, no new logic
duplicated.

Deliberately stopped short of building v7's full detection-speed/confluence-entry measurement --
it needs the 6 raw indicator values recomputed at an arbitrary point in history, and every place
that computation already lives in the file is its own separate hand-written copy with no shared
function to call. Building a fourth copy just for this would be exactly the kind of duplicated-logic
problem the charter itself warns against. This turns out to be the same underlying fix (unifying
the scoring logic into one real path) already flagged as the next big lever after tonight's ratchet
work -- so that one refactor, done carefully, unlocks both fronts at once. Noted clearly in the
installed skill file so it doesn't get worked around by accident later.
